payoff: AI saw where the hurricane would hit when standard forecasts didn't
means: Google's AI called Hurricane Isaias's Florida landfall when the usual physics-based models pointed elsewhere. Better track forecasts mean earlier, better-aimed evacuation warnings. It was weaker than the Hurricane Center's own forecast on how strong the storm would be.
try: Google's Weather Lab shows its AI storm forecasts live (free, Google sign-in)
people: Families on the coast deciding whether, and when, to evacuate.

payoff: An AI solved 8 in 10 of medicine's hardest diagnosis puzzles. Doctors solved fewer than 4
means: On 304 of the toughest published cases, Microsoft's diagnostic AI was right 83% of the time, against 36% for general doctors, in a study in the journal Science. People with rare, hard-to-name illnesses could get answers faster. It is not available to patients yet; a hospital trial comes next.
people: Patients with rare, hard-to-name illnesses who can wait years for an answer.

payoff: A free map now shows every forest on Earth, down to a 10-metre patch
means: Google DeepMind's map sorts the world's forests into six types, such as natural or planted, about 90% accurately, checked at more than 9,000 sites. That makes it far harder to pass off a plantation as old forest, or to hide clearing.
try: The map is free to explore on Google Earth Engine
people: Forest communities, and anyone checking a 'deforestation-free' label on what they buy.

payoff: Anthropic says its AI checked the code inside 123 widely used programs and found hundreds of hidden bugs
means: Anthropic says its AI mathematically checked the building blocks that many apps and websites rely on, and found defects some of which had gone unnoticed for years. Bugs like these are how hackers get in, so finding them first makes the software you use safer. This is Anthropic's own account so far.
people: Everyone who uses the apps and websites built on that code.

payoff: OpenAI says its AI cracked three problems that stumped mathematicians and physicists for decades
means: If the claims hold, AI is starting to do original science, not just summarize it. The math proofs have been checked by computer; leading experts are now reviewing the computing and physics claims in the open.

payoff: AI now helps decide when patients are ready to go home at 12 Virginia hospitals
means: Sentara uses an AI tool to watch patients and flag who is ready to leave, across all 12 of its Virginia hospitals. That can free beds and nurses' time. The hospital group says no jobs are cut; its estimate of hours saved is still a forecast.
people: Patients waiting to go home, and nurses short on time.

payoff: Axiom says its AI agents checked one of math's biggest proofs, 15,000 pages long, in 24 days
means: Axiom says dozens of its AI agents, directed by engineers and mathematicians, turned the classification of finite simple groups into about 43 million lines a computer can check step by step, finding 34 departures from the published proofs, mostly minor. The proof itself was never in doubt. No outside group has rebuilt it yet; Axiom has published the files so others can.
people: Mathematicians who build on results too long for any one person to check.

payoff: An AI found pancreatic cancer on scans doctors had read as clear, a median of 475 days before diagnosis
means: The study used earlier CT scans of 219 people later diagnosed with pancreatic cancer. On the scans held back for testing, the model caught 73% of the cancers; specialist radiologists caught 38.9%. The study is peer-reviewed, in the journal Gut. The catch: it looked back at old scans, its patients lacked ethnic diversity, and it needs forward-looking trials before doctors can use it.
people: People with pancreatic cancer, which is usually found too late to cure

payoff: Anthropic says its AI found 62 serious Chrome flaws, now fixed before attackers used them
means: Anthropic says an unreleased model, after initial prompting, found flaws and chained them into working attacks on Chrome, Safari, Android, Windows and Linux; it reported them and all are patched, with no real-world attacks. That is the company's account: The Hacker News found some public flaw records don't clearly match its descriptions. The same skill in the wrong hands is the warning.
people: Everyone using Chrome, whose browser got 62 critical or high fixes
